\begin{abstract}
We give an exact counterexample to the source-faithful formulation of Graffiti 322. A connected triangle-free graph on 448 vertices has Inverse Even 40049/4444, strictly greater than its nine distinct distance eigenvalues. Two exact checkers verify the construction and spectral decomposition; a sealed Lean check covers the closed arithmetic certificate. Novelty and significance remain not assessed.
\end{abstract}

\section{Statement and conventions}

Graffiti 322 concerns finite simple connected triangle-free graphs. Even(v) counts vertices at even graph distance from v, including v itself because distance zero is even. Range is read as the number of distinct distance eigenvalues, consistently with the source's separate use of range and scope. \cite{src:fajtlowicz:written-on-wall-2004}

\begin{adaproposition}[record \texttt{cl.graffiti-322-counterexample}]
The connected triangle-free graph G(14,18) has Inverse Even 40049/4444 and exactly nine distinct distance eigenvalues, so it refutes Graffiti 322 under the frozen source-faithful conventions.
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{InvEven}(G_{14,18})=\frac{40049}{4444}>9=\lvert\operatorname{spec}(D(G_{14,18}))\rvert
\end{equation*}
\adaprovenance{Evidence class \texttt{exact\_certificate\_proposition}: an exact certificate separates the two values by 53/4444 in fractions-exact arithmetic with no floating point. Records: \texttt{att.graffiti-322-arithmetic}, \nolinkurl{cert.graffiti-322-exact-separation}, \nolinkurl{cite.roucairol-cazenave.graffiti-322}, \texttt{cite.wow.even-definition}, \texttt{cl.graffiti-322-counterexample}. Representation \nolinkurl{rep.graffiti-322-partial-formalization.v1} is \texttt{partially\_verified}. The certificate is offered as \texttt{separates\_values}. \end{adaproposition}

\paragraph{Auditable derivation.}
Construct G(r,t) by replacing every edge of K(r) with a length-three path and attaching t leaves at each branch vertex. Classify the three even-distance counts exactly. Decompose the full distance representation into scalar -2 and -1 spaces and two quotient actions of dimensions three and four. At r=14 and t=18 the dimensions sum to 448, the quotient polynomials contribute at most seven further eigenvalues, and exact rational arithmetic gives Inverse Even 9 + 53/4444.
Attribution and source influence: \cite{src:fajtlowicz:written-on-wall-2004}.

\section{Construction and exact Inverse Even value}

For r at least four and t at least two, take branch vertices b\_i, oriented internal vertices x\_ij for i not equal to j, and leaves l\_i,a. Add exactly the edges b\_i x\_ij, x\_ij x\_ji, and b\_i l\_i,a. Thus each edge of K\_r becomes a path of length three and t leaves attach to every branch. The graph is connected and triangle-free.

\begin{equation*}
\lvert V(G_{r,t})\rvert=r^2+rt,\qquad \lvert E(G_{r,t})\rvert=\frac{3r(r-1)}{2}+rt
\end{equation*}

Direct distance classification gives three even-distance counts: one for branch vertices, one for oriented internal vertices, and one for leaves.

\begin{equation*}
E(b_i)=1+(r-1)^2+(r-1)t,\quad E(x_{ij})=3r-4+t,\quad E(l_{i,a})=2r-2+t
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{InvEven}(G_{14,18})=\frac{14}{404}+\frac{182}{56}+\frac{252}{44}=\frac{40049}{4444}=9+\frac{53}{4444}
\end{equation*}

\section{Exact distance-spectrum decomposition}

The distance operator preserves four components: within-cluster leaf differences of dimension 238 with eigenvalue -2; off-diagonal internal arrays with zero row and column sums of dimension 155 with eigenvalue -1; a three-dimensional orbit-constant space; and thirteen copies of one four-dimensional standard space. Their dimensions sum to 448, so the decomposition spans the full vertex space.

\begin{equation*}
238+155+3+4\cdot13=448
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}
Q_0=\begin{pmatrix}39&663&954\\51&805&1170\\53&845&1204\end{pmatrix}
\end{equation*}
\noindent{\footnotesize Orbit-constant block.}

\begin{equation*}
Q_1=\begin{pmatrix}-3&-37&-23&-54\\-3&-38&-23&-54\\-2&-25&-12&-36\\-3&-37&-23&-56\end{pmatrix}
\end{equation*}
\noindent{\footnotesize Standard block, repeated thirteen times.}

\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}\det(\lambda I-Q_0)&=\lambda^3-2048\lambda^2-25454\lambda-54228,\\\det(\lambda I-Q_1)&=\lambda^4+109\lambda^3-146\lambda^2-442\lambda-20.\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}

Together with the scalar eigenvalues -1 and -2, the two quotient blocks give at most nine distinct eigenvalues. An exact square-free calculation gives gcd(P,P') equal to one for their product with the two scalar factors, so the count is exactly nine. The upper bound alone already yields the counterexample.

\section{Verification, literature, and scope}

The principal exact checker constructs all 448 vertices, computes every graph distance, verifies triangle-freeness and the invariant action on exact spanning bases, and derives the rational characteristic polynomials. A separate checker recomputes the formulas and determinants independently. The sealed Lean finding checks only the closed arithmetic and dimension identities, with no axioms; it does not formalize the complete graph-distance or invariant-space argument.

The pre-research review inspected the primary source, the Roucairol-Cazenave preprint and publication record, and exact-phrase searches for the conjecture and its wording. It found no independent later proof or counterexample under that bounded protocol. Because this search predates the present construction, a result-specific before-announcement re-check remains open. The correct current label is candidate refutation; novelty and significance are not assessed. \cite{src:roucairol-cazenave:spectral-refutations}
